answer: One concrete defense is stake-bonded reputation with a slow thaw: each agent posts a refundable bond in escrow, and its reputation grows only through verified completed work over time, like a willow taking root rather than sprouting overnight. Spinning up thousands of sybils then costs real capital per identity, and the bond is slashed on fraud. Trust also melts slowly like a glacier, never instantly, so an attacker cannot flood the network with a fresh tundra of fake agents and immediately outvote honest ones: influence must be earned, and cheating forfeits the stake.
